As outlined in the report, while the city's current budgeting approach has done a good job of keeping overall expenditure increases below inflation and growth and lower than other orders of government.
The existing approach offers little insight into the budgeting priorities of the city, other than maintaining the existing service levels across the board.

Implementing a priority based budgeting tool would offer additional insight into which services and programs are of highest priority for the city and assist in future decision making and allocations. Next slide please.

Developing a priority based budgeting tool is typically accomplished through a five step process. Step one is identifying your overall program inventory. Currently the city reports out on 87 different service lines. However, a priority based budget would break this down further into detailed program levels.
Step two involves properly costing out the details of this program inventory and followed by step three which is developing the priorities on which programs will be scored against.
Typical scoring metrics include does this program align or contribute towards the achievement of city council strategic priorities.
Is the city mandated to provide the service. Is there a reliance on the city to provide the service and how much of the community is utilizing this service.
Step four then takes those metrics and scores each program identified against those.
Finally step five is to take action with the developed prioritization list.
It is important to note that a priority based budgeting tool does not make resource allocation decisions for city council or administration.
It simply provides a tool and additional insight for those decisions to be made. Next slide please.
With that being said, there are several benefits and challenges to be aware of when developing regarding when developing a priority based budget.
Some of the key benefits include that it identifies and clearly communicates the budget priorities for the city.
It prioritizes individual programs rather than service lines or departments and facilitates better budget discussions.
However, there are some challenges with a priority based budgeting that committee should be aware of.
With lower tiered priorities, partners or service providers may feel marginalized and less committed to partnering with the city if they're identified as a lower priority.
Expectations of the process and actual outcomes may not align with the public or city council and requires identifying what is not critically important, which can be difficult. Next slide please.

In terms of others who have used this approach, while priority based budgeting has been around for some time, there are limited recent examples of municipalities and Canada that have utilized this approach.
Edmonton is the most relevant example who implemented a priority based budgeting approach as part of their 23 to 26 operating budget and plan.
The report includes further detail on their journey and reports that were presented to their council. Next slide please.
We've included in the report our four options on how to proceed. These include not implementing a priority based budget limited implementation, a full implementation or a targeted implementation.
Overall, the administration does see value in the approach and is recommending option three, the full implementation of a priority based budget for the 2027 cycle.
While a pilot or targeted implementation typically makes sense for projects such as these to trial.
Limiting the scope to a few business lines or not fully implementing the approach really limits the value of a priority based budget in perspective of the administration.
